Three runtime traps in `bun build --compile` binaries (bit v1.0.0-beta.2, fixed beta.3):
1. NODE_ENV defaults to "development" at RUNTIME even though --compile implies --production at build time — any NODE_ENV === 'development' check trips.
2. __dirname is baked at COMPILE time (the build-host path, e.g. the GitHub Actions runner path); import.meta.dir returns /$bunfs/root. Never compute runtime paths from either.
3. process.argv[0] is the literal string "bun", argv[1] is /$bunfs/<build-time-outfile>. Use process.execPath for the actual invoked path; argv.slice(2) arg parsing works Node-style (Commander fine).

DETECTION: process.argv[1]?.startsWith('/$bunfs/') === "inside a bun-compiled binary" — short-circuit dev-mode/argv/__dirname logic on it. os.homedir(), process.env.HOME, and fs.* against the host filesystem all work normally (/$bunfs/ only applies to bundled-source paths).

VALIDATION LESSON: smoke-testing only --version + build-matrix success missed all three. Runtime-affecting release validation must exercise: a data-dir write (any set op), MCP framing (initialize + tools/list + one tool call), and stdout piping (`rvr --version | head -1` prints exactly the version).
